text: Strategy. Our strategy is to grow in the middle market.
Approach. Their approach is slower but safer.
Insight. The best insight came from the smallest team.
Sector. Our sector moves more slowly than technology.
Scale. The scale is different, but the problem is the same.
Sustainable. Growing that fast is not sustainable.
Trend. The trend is better than the number.
Trade-off. Speed or safety, that is the trade-off.
Your market is much bigger than mine, so I am not sure we can compare.
The scale is different. The problem is the same.
Go on.
We both have too many small clients and not enough people. Unlike you, we cannot say no to any of them.
So what is your strategy?
Grow the middle, drop nothing. It is slower than yours, but it is more sustainable.
It is also more expensive.
That is the trade-off. We pay in cost, you pay in relationships.
Fair. Honestly, that is the best insight I have heard today.
Say that again on Thursday, in front of the panel.
The scale is different, but the problem is the same.
Compared to last year, the number is worse and the business is better.
Their approach is slower, but it is more sustainable.
That is the trade-off.
And you? How does that compare to your market?

Let me put the two years side by side, because the headline number is misleading. Last year we grew eight percent. This year we grew four. So on paper, this year is worse. But last year we grew by adding clients we should never have taken, and half of them are gone now. This year the growth is smaller, and it is entirely from clients we already had. Compared to last year, the number is worse and the business is better. My point is that the trend matters more than the number, and the most expensive mistake in my sector is to celebrate the wrong one.

I want to push back on that, politely. You said the American model is the most efficient, and by one measure it is. It is faster, and it is cheaper per transaction. But efficiency is not the only thing we are buying. Unlike the American model, the European one keeps the client relationship inside the bank, and that is worth something the spreadsheet does not show. So I would not say one is better than the other. I would say they are optimised for different things, and the trade-off is between speed and closeness. Whichever you pick, you are giving something up.
